articles.body: NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles! A passenger traveling on a Carnival Panorama cruise jumped overboard as the ship was wrapping up the last full day of a week-long sailing. The cruise departed Long Beach, California, on September 13 and was headed back there from Puerto Vallarta, Mexico , when a male passenger jumped overboard, according to the cruise line. "Carnival Cruise Line confirmed Saturday that a male guest aboard Carnival Panorama jumped overboard while the ship was sailing from Puerto Vallarta, Mexico to Long Beach, California," a Carnival Cruise Line spokesperson told Fox News Digital. CRUISE PASSENGER HAILED AS HERO AFTER JUMPING INTO WATER TO SAVE 84-YEAR-OLD MAN A passenger traveling on a Carnival Panorama cruise jumped overboard as the ship was wrapping up the last full day of a week-long sailing. (Brittany Murray/MediaNews Group/Long Beach Press-Telegram) "When notified of a missing guest, the ship's team initiated search and investigation procedures, including reviewing CCTV footage and notifying both the U.S. and Mexico Coast Guards," the statement continued. The spokesperson said the company is providing support to the family who was traveling with the guest. "Our thoughts and prayers are with them and their loved ones," the statement reads. CARNIVAL CRUISE PASSENGER, 67, FOUND DEAD WHILE SNORKELING OFF THE COAST OF AUSTRALIA DURING EXCURSION Carnival Panorama sails near Los Cabos, Baja California Sur, Mexico, on Aug. 3, 2023. (ALFREDO ESTRELLA/AFP via Getty Images) According to a Reddit user who said they were aboard the sailing, announcements regarding a missing guest were heard at around 11 a.m. on Saturday. Carnival Panorama had departed from its last port of call on the sail, Puerto Vallarta, at 8 p.m. on Thursday. The call for the missing guest was repeated several times over the next several hours. At about 3 p.m., the ship reportedly turned around. Another announcement was made at about 3:30 p.m. that there would be a shipwide search, and all guests were told to return to their staterooms. Security visited each of the staterooms to scan guests' ship identification cards, which is a standard procedure in the event of a search. Carnival Panorama had departed from its last port of call on the sail, Puerto Vallarta, at 8 p.m. on Thursday. (Brittany Murray/MediaNews Group/Long Beach Press-Telegram via Getty Images) An hour later, another announcement suggested the search was continuing, and guests were instructed to remain in their staterooms. At around 5 p.m., the captain and cruise director said the guest had been confirmed overboard after a review of onboard cameras, adding that local authorities would continue the search and rescue operation and guests were no longer required to stay in their staterooms. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The family and traveling companions of the missing guest were notified of his disappearance and were offered support from the care team. Shortly after 7 p.m., guests were told that the ship was expected to reach Long Beach at 9 a.m. Fox News' Jessica Mekles contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Confirmed: PBOC leaves Loan Prime Rates unchanged in September
articles.summary: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC), China's central bank, announced to leave its Loan Prime Rates (LPRs) unchanged on Monday. The one-year and five-year LPRs were at 3.00% and 3.50%, respectively.
articles.body: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC), China's central bank, announced to leave its Loan Prime Rates (LPRs) unchanged on Monday. The one-year and five-year LPRs were at 3.00% and 3.50%, respectively. Market reaction to the PBoC interest rate decision At the time of writing, the AUD/USD is trading 0.03% higher on the day to trade at 0.7127. PBOC FAQs The primary monetary policy objectives of the People's Bank of China (PBoC) are to safeguard price stability, including exchange rate stability, and promote economic growth. China’s central bank also aims to implement financial reforms, such as opening and developing the financial market. The PBoC is owned by the state of the People's Republic of China (PRC), so it is not considered an autonomous institution. The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) Committee Secretary, nominated by the Chairman of the State Council, has a key influence on the PBoC’s management and direction, not the governor. However, Mr. Pan Gongsheng currently holds both of these posts. Unlike the Western economies, the PBoC uses a broader set of monetary policy instruments to achieve its objectives. The primary tools include a seven-day Reverse Repo Rate (RRR), Medium-term Lending Facility (MLF), foreign exchange interventions and Reserve Requirement Ratio (RRR). However, The Loan Prime Rate (LPR) is China’s benchmark interest rate. Changes to the LPR directly influence the rates that need to be paid in the market for loans and mortgages and the interest paid on savings. By changing the LPR, China’s central bank can also influence the exchange rates of the Chinese Renminbi. Yes, China has 19 private banks – a small fraction of the financial system. The largest private banks are digital lenders WeBank and MYbank, which are backed by tech giants Tencent and Ant Group, per The Straits Times. In 2014, China allowed domestic lenders fully capitalized by private funds to operate in the state-dominated financial sector.

articles.headline: Nvidia boss rejects AI extinction fears as 'doomsday narratives'
articles.summary: minutes agoOsmond ChiaBusiness reporterBloomberg via Getty ImagesNvidia CEO Jensen Huang has described warnings that AI could lead to humanity's extinction by the next decade as "doomsday narratives"."2030...
articles.body: 8 minutes ago Osmond Chia Business reporter Bloomberg via Getty Images Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has described warnings that AI could lead to humanity's extinction by the next decade as "doomsday narratives". "2030 is not going to be the end of the world. There is 0% chance that's going to be the end of the world", Huang said in an interview with CBS News, the BBC's US partner. Huang added: "Scaring people is unnecessary. It is irresponsible." Warnings from researchers in recent weeks about potential risks posed by the technology escalated the debate about AI safety, with some industry executives calling for a slowdown in developing models. Coxon's concerns sparked debate about the technology's risks, including calls by top executives like Anthropic boss Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman urging for AI's development to slow down. Huang said that such predictions are "not grounded in science", adding that it is in Nvidia's best interest to ensure the industry builds its products responsibly. "Our company's success is directly connected to the safe deployment of products and services," he said. "If we don't continue to do that, our value would be diminished." Huang suggested AI firms talking about a "slow down" could be seeking liability protections for harms their products may cause. "Go and read between the lines," he said. "They're actually not asking for more laws. They're asking to be relieved of the laws we do have, and I think that that's a problem." Nvidia is a key player in the industry, developing cutting edge computer chips that are crucial for making AI models. Last week, Huang appeared at a UK summit hosted by King Charles, who warned tech leaders of the "existential dangers" of AI. "The task before you is not merely to advance technology, but to ensure that it remains firmly in the service of humanity, community and the natural world," the King told the group. Trump made a surprise phone call to Huang while the Nvidia boss was speaking on stage at a tech conference in Los Angeles on 14 September. During the call, Trump criticised calls to slow the pace of AI development and dismissed fears as a "hoax".

articles.headline: Volatile yen draws intervention watch, other currencies subdued
articles.summary: Markets focused on the yen on Monday following a sharp drop last week that spurred speculation of a rate check, while investors pondered rate outlooks after hikes from major central banks last week.
articles.body: Currency markets focused on the yen on Monday following a sharp drop last week that spurred speculation of a rate check from Tokyo, while investors pondered interest-rate outlooks after a wave of hikes from major central banks last week. Sheldon Cooper | Lightrocket | Getty Images Currency markets focused on the yen on Monday following a sharp drop last week that spurred speculation of a rate check from Tokyo, while investors pondered interest-rate outlooks after a wave of hikes from major central banks last week. The yen was a touch firmer at 156.64 per US dollar after dropping 2% last week. Japan markets were closed for a three-day holiday, leading to low liquidity while keeping traders on alert for an official intervention to prop up the volatile currency. The Bank of Japan raised rates on Friday to their highest level in 31 years to 1.25%, yet the widely expected move did not boost the yen as two dissenting votes and a lack of explicitly hawkish guidance disappointed investors. That led to the yen sharply declining before the Nikkei newspaper reported that Japanese officials conducted rate checks. A rate check involves authorities asking banks for currency quotes to gauge market conditions, which traders view as a precursor to currency intervention. Apart from the BOJ, the Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank raised rates this month, with both warning further tightening might be needed to tackle inflation due to the almost seven-month-long war in the Middle East. Fred Neumann, chief Asia economist at HSBC, said the BOJ's messaging has become all the harder because the Fed delivered a hawkish signal with its unanimous decision to raise its policy rate. The yen had firmed to its strongest level in seven months in early September as traders wagered on a faster pace of BOJ hikes and early signs of repatriation by Japanese investors but has since surrendered some of those gains. "The bar thus remains high for the BOJ to convince markets of its hawkish tilt and anchor expectations when it comes to the yen," Neumann said. "In the coming weeks and months, investors may again test the resolve of the BOJ to push rates higher and match the Fed's tightening." The euro was little changed at $1.1482 after voting projections showed the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) took first place in state elections in northeastern Germany, in a blow to Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservative party. ING economists said the results clearly echo the low popularity of the entire federal government, and of Chancellor Friedrich Merz in particular. "Years of economic stagnation helped produce that fragmentation. Now the fragmentation will make the stagnation harder to escape," they said in a note. The dollar index , which tracks the US currency against six major peers, was steady at 100.23 after gaining more than 1% last week following the Fed's rate hike, as the central bank signalled more increases could be coming. Traders are currently pricing in a 55% chance of a rate hike at the Fed's next meeting in October, up from 42.5% a week earlier, the CME FedWatch tool showed. "We do not think that the midterm elections are going to be a limiting factor in the Fed delivering another hike in October," said Thomas Simons, chief US economist at Jefferies. "Whether there is another hike in December will come down to the data and geopolitical developments. Looking to 2027, the path of rates will come down to what happens with the labor market. We would say rate cuts are likely in second half of 2027." In other currencies, sterling last bought $1.339 in early trading. The Australian dollar fetched $0.7129, while the New Zealand dollar was at $0.5721.

articles.headline: New Zealand Dollar languishes near two-month low vs USD as bears await break below 0.5700
articles.summary: The NZD/USD pair attracts some sellers for the second straight day and trades around the 0.5720-0.5715 zone during the Asian session on Monday, well within striking distance of an over two-month low set last week.
articles.body: The NZD/USD pair attracts some sellers for the second straight day and trades around the 0.5720-0.5715 zone during the Asian session on Monday, well within striking distance of an over two-month low set last week. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) continues with its relative underperformance on the back of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's (RBNZ) dovish rate hike amid weak domestic growth. In contrast, the US Federal Reserve (Fed) maintained a relatively hawkish stance and signaled at least one more follow-up move this year after raising rates for the first time in three years last week. This, along with geopolitical uncertainties, acts as a tailwind for the safe-haven US Dollar (USD) and weighs on the NZD/USD pair. Nordea sees stronger case for tighter Fed policy as US resilience persists Economists at Nordea highlight that the US economy “remains resilient,” with “inflationary pressures” showing “few signs of easing” and the labour market “also holding up well.” In their view, this combination strengthens “the case for a more restrictive monetary policy stance.” Nordea reiterates that it “maintain[s] our forecast for two more hikes,” but cautions that “we see the risks as tilted to the upside,” underscoring the possibility that the Fed may ultimately need to do more than currently anticipated. In the latest developments surrounding the Middle East crisis, Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen said that they attacked sensitive sites in the Saudi capital of Riyadh on Saturday with missiles and drones. Moreover, Iran laid out seven conditions – including an end to the war on all fronts, the release of frozen Iranian assets and the lifting of the US naval blockade on Iranian ports – for restarting negotiations with the US. This keeps geopolitical risk premium in play and continues to support the Greenback. Meanwhile, a recovery in shipments from Saudi Arabia dragged oil prices to an over one-week low, helping alleviate immediate fears of runaway inflation. This keeps US bond yields below a multi-year high touched last week and holds back USD bulls from placing aggressive bets. Traders also seem hesitant ahead of a meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping on Thursday, which will provide a fresh impetus to antipodean currencies, including the Kiwi. NZD/USD daily chart Technical Analysis The NZD/USD pair keeps a bearish near-term tone, awaiting a break below the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement support near the 0.5700 mark. This would expose the deeper Fibonacci floor near 0.5624. On the topside, initial resistance emerges at the 61.8% Fibo. retracement near 0.5763, followed by the 50.0% level at 0.5806. Above that, a dense barrier is formed by the 38.2% retracement at 0.5849 and the 200-day SMA at 0.5853, ahead of the 23.6% level at 0.5902 and the recent swing high around 0.5988. (The technical analysis of this story was written with the help of an AI tool. Know more. ) The New Zealand Dollar (NZD), also known as the Kiwi, is a well-known traded currency among investors. Its value is broadly determined by the health of the New Zealand economy and the country’s central bank policy. Still, there are some unique particularities that also can make NZD move. The performance of the Chinese economy tends to move the Kiwi because China is New Zealand’s biggest trading partner. Bad news for the Chinese economy likely means less New Zealand exports to the country, hitting the economy and thus its currency. Another factor moving NZD is dairy prices as the dairy industry is New Zealand’s main export. High dairy prices boost export income, contributing positively to the economy and thus to the NZD. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) aims to achieve and maintain an inflation rate between 1% and 3% over the medium term, with a focus to keep it near the 2% mid-point. To this end, the bank sets an appropriate level of interest rates. When inflation is too high, the RBNZ will increase interest rates to cool the economy, but the move will also make bond yields higher, increasing investors’ appeal to invest in the country and thus boosting NZD. On the contrary, lower interest rates tend to weaken NZD. The so-called rate differential, or how rates in New Zealand are or are expected to be compared to the ones set by the US Federal Reserve, can also play a key role in moving the NZD/USD pair. Macroeconomic data releases in New Zealand are key to assess the state of the economy and can impact the New Zealand Dollar’s (NZD) valuation. A strong economy, based on high economic growth, low unemployment and high confidence is good for NZD. High economic growth attracts foreign investment and may encourage the Reserve Bank of New Zealand to increase interest rates, if this economic strength comes together with elevated inflation. Conversely, if economic data is weak, NZD is likely to depreciate. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) tends to strengthen during risk-on periods, or when investors perceive that broader market risks are low and are optimistic about growth. This tends to lead to a more favorable outlook for commodities and so-called ‘commodity currencies’ such as the Kiwi. Conversely, NZD tends to weaken at times of market turbulence or economic uncertainty as investors tend to sell higher-risk assets and flee to the more-stable safe havens.

On the contrary, lower interest rates tend to weaken NZD. The so-called rate differential, or how rates in New Zealand are or are expected to be compared to the ones set by the US Federal Reserve, can also play a key role in moving the NZD/USD pair. Macroeconomic data releases in New Zealand are key to assess the state of the economy and can impact the New Zealand Dollar’s (NZD) valuation. A strong economy, based on high economic growth, low unemployment and high confidence is good for NZD. High economic growth attracts foreign investment and may encourage the Reserve Bank of New Zealand to increase interest rates, if this economic strength comes together with elevated inflation. Conversely, if economic data is weak, NZD is likely to depreciate. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) tends to strengthen during risk-on periods, or when investors perceive that broader market risks are low and are optimistic about growth. This tends to lead to a more favorable outlook for commodities and so-called ‘commodity currencies’ such as the Kiwi. Conversely, NZD tends to weaken at times of market turbulence or economic uncertainty as investors tend to sell higher-risk assets and flee to the more-stable safe havens.

articles.headline: Japanese Yen bulls seem hesitant amid BoJ's dovish rate hike as Fed bets support USD
articles.summary: The USD/JPY pair attracts some sellers following a modest Asian session uptick to the 157.10 area and moves away from a two-week high, touched on Friday in reaction to the Bank of Japan's (BoJ) dovish rate hike.
articles.body: The USD/JPY pair attracts some sellers following a modest Asian session uptick to the 157.10 area and moves away from a two-week high, touched on Friday in reaction to the Bank of Japan's (BoJ) dovish rate hike. Spot prices currently trade around the 156.75 region, though the near-term bias seems tilted in favor of bullish traders. As was widely expected, the Japanese central bank raised the short-term interest rate to a 31-year high on Friday and reiterated that it will continue raising rates in response to developments in activity, prices and financial conditions. However, the 7-2 vote split pointed to a divided board, which, along with data showing that inflation in Japan eased slightly in August, tempered bets for a more aggressive tightening cycle. This, in turn, is seen as undermining the Japanese Yen (JPY) and acting as a tailwind for the USD/JPY pair. Meanwhile, a further escalation of tensions in the Middle East and the growing risk of a broader regional conflict help the safe-haven US Dollar (USD) stall its retracement slide from the highest level since late July, set on Friday. In the latest development, Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen said that they attacked sensitive sites in the Saudi capital of Riyadh on Saturday with missiles and drones. Moreover, Iran laid out seven conditions for restarting talks with the US, which keeps the geopolitical risk premium firmly in play. Adding to this, the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) hawkish outlook , signaling at least one more follow-up rate hike this year, acts as a tailwind for the Greenback and the USD/JPY pair. Traders, however, seem reluctant to place aggressive bullish bets and opt to wait for further developments surrounding the Middle East crisis. This week's focus will also be on a crucial meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping on Thursday, which will influence risk sentiment and drive the USD. USD/JPY 4-hour chart Technical Analysis The USD/JPY keeps a capped tone below the 200-period Simple Moving Average (SMA) on the 4-hour chart, at 157.61. Moreover, spot prices have slipped back under the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement at 157.49, leaving that level and the nearby 200-period SMA as a dense overhead barrier that suggests rallies are likely to meet selling interest. A decisively move beyond this zone, however, should pave the way for gains to the 78.6% retracement near 158.75 and the recent swing high at 160.36. On the downside, initial support emerges at the 50.0% retracement around 156.60, with additional cushions at the 38.2% level near 155.72 and the 23.6% retracement at 154.62, while a deeper pullback could expose the Fibonacci anchor at 152.85. (The technical analysis of this story was written with the help of an AI tool. Know more. ) The Japanese Yen (JPY) is one of the world’s most traded currencies. Its value is broadly determined by the performance of the Japanese economy, but more specifically by the Bank of Japan’s policy, the differential between Japanese and US bond yields, or risk sentiment among traders, among other factors. One of the Bank of Japan’s mandates is currency control, so its moves are key for the Yen. The BoJ has directly intervened in currency markets sometimes, generally to lower the value of the Yen, although it refrains from doing it often due to political concerns of its main trading partners. The BoJ ultra-loose monetary policy between 2013 and 2024 caused the Yen to depreciate against its main currency peers due to an increasing policy divergence between the Bank of Japan and other main central banks. More recently, the gradually unwinding of this ultra-loose policy has given some support to the Yen. Over the last decade, the BoJ’s stance of sticking to ultra-loose monetary policy has led to a widening policy divergence with other central banks, particularly with the US Federal Reserve. This supported a widening of the differential between the 10-year US and Japanese bonds, which favored the US Dollar against the Japanese Yen. The BoJ decision in 2024 to gradually abandon the ultra-loose policy, coupled with interest-rate cuts in other major central banks, is narrowing this differential. The Japanese Yen is often seen as a safe-haven investment. This means that in times of market stress, investors are more likely to put their money in the Japanese currency due to its supposed reliability and stability. Turbulent times are likely to strengthen the Yen’s value against other currencies seen as more risky to invest in.

articles.headline: Bessent: US proposes AI incident alert system in talks with China
articles.summary: MATT SEDENSKYUpdated Mon, September 21, 2026 at 1:49 AM UTC1 min readIn this photo taken with a smartphone, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, left, and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, address...
articles.body: MATT SEDENSKY Updated Mon, September 21, 2026 at 1:49 AM UTC 1 min read In this photo taken with a smartphone, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, left, and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, address reporters in New York, Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026. (AP Photo/Matt Sedensky) NEW YORK (AP) — Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Sunday the U.S. has proposed a new "notification mechanism" for artificial intelligence incidents that could affect national security, part of weekend discussions ahead of talks at the White House this week between President Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping . "We want a shared vision of common goals and common threats," Bessent told reporters after talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York. "We think that just like any cross-border activity, that moving from opaque to more transparency between the No. 1 and the No. 2 AI powers in the world is very important." Trump has resisted calls to slow down AI development , saying that would help China catch up to U.S. companies. Standing together in the soaring lobby of the JPMorgan Chase headquarters late Sunday, Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the groundwork had been laid for talks between Xi and Trump set to take place on Thursday. They said the two sides had agreed to operationalize a new "Board of Trade" that the two leaders had discussed when they met in Beijing in May. "Today those notions have become reality," Greer said. Greer said the countries were still discussing what "nonsensitive" items could be considered for lower tariffs, but that the list could potentially include consumer and agricultural goods, energy products and medical devices.

articles.headline: IMF Says Global Public Debt at Record High, Governments Falling Short on Deficit Cuts
articles.summary: The IMF said global **public debt** is projected to exceed 100% of **GDP** by 2029 and that countries need **fiscal consolidation**. Georgieva said U.S. **fiscal deficits** and **debt** are not sustainable and stressed the need for a gradual reduction. The IMF said persistent **inflation** and the possibility of further **interest-rate hikes** could increase government borrowing costs and **debt burdens**.
articles.body: Suehyeon Lee Summary The IMF said global public debt is projected to exceed 100% of GDP by 2029 and that countries need fiscal consolidation . Georgieva said U.S. fiscal deficits and debt are not sustainable and stressed the need for a gradual reduction. The IMF said persistent inflation and the possibility of further interest-rate hikes could increase government borrowing costs and debt burdens . Forecast Trend Report by Period Photo: ChatGPT The International Monetary Fund urged governments to accelerate efforts to reduce fiscal deficits and debt as global public debt has climbed to a record high. Bloomberg reported on September 20 that IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva, speaking at the Qatar Economic Forum in New York, said she had long warned that fiscal consolidation was essential. While awareness of the issue is rising, actual policy action remains insufficient, she said. The IMF projects global public debt will exceed 100% of gross domestic product by 2029. That would come two years earlier than previously expected, with rising debt in the U.S. and China cited as the main reason. Georgieva singled out the U.S. fiscal position. She said she has repeatedly urged close scrutiny of the country's finances and, through conversations with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, confirmed there is recognition that the current trajectory is not sustainable and that the U.S. needs to gradually reduce its fiscal deficit and debt. Last month, Georgieva also warned that the rising debt path of major advanced economies, including the U.S., required a policy response. She also said high inflation and interest rates could increase debt burdens across countries. Inflation remains "persistent," Georgieva said, adding that central banks around the world may need to follow the Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank in raising benchmark interest rates. Any further increases would raise government borrowing costs and interest payments on existing debt. Georgieva also referred to the economic shock from energy and transport disruptions in the Middle East. She said commodity-producing countries such as Qatar, Kuwait and Iraq are being affected and could face a sharp economic contraction. Still, she said Qatar's fiscal buffers built up over time are protecting the economy for now. The IMF forecasts Qatar's economy will contract 8.6% this year, a sharp reversal from the 6.1% growth it had projected before the war with Iran. Longer-term uncertainty surrounding the liquefied natural gas market was also cited as a risk to Qatar's economy. Georgieva said monetary policy in emerging markets is now comparable to, or in some cases stronger than, that in advanced economies, again emphasizing the need for fiscal discipline in developed countries where debt has risen sharply. A demo for the title has just been added to the Nintendo eShop, so hop on your Switch 2 and snag it now! That demo has also paved the way for a comparison video between the PS5 and Switch 2 versions of the game, and you can check it out above. In Stellar Blade: Complete Edition, step into the role of EVE, an elite warrior sent to reclaim Earth from mysterious forces. Experience intense combat and a twisting plot as you unravel the mysteries of Earth’s downfall in an immersive sci-fi world. Featuring a blend of cinematic storytelling and gameplay, Stellar Blade offers deep character progression with customizable skills, gear, and combat builds – which you’ll need during epic boss encounters. Further, players can experience support for Joy-Con 2 motion controls for activities, adding in an extra layer of immersion to moments away from combat. Stellar Blade Complete Edition will also include four new couture outfits inspired by Bayonetta. All four will be available for free on Nintendo Switch 2 starting Nov. 5th, 2026 alongside the game’s launch. Pre-orders for Stellar Blade Complete Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 are live on the eShop and at participating retailers. Players who pre-order will receive an early unlock of the Planet Diving Suit (White Edition), Classic Round Glasses, and Ear Armor Earrings for EVE. A Limited Edition SteelBook, featuring exclusive new key art, is also available to pre-order today through participating retailers and Panax, in strictly limited quantities. The Complete Edition includes all previously released content, including the NieR:Automata and GODDESS OF VICTORY: NIKKE DLC, as well as additional Complete Edition bonuses (Stargazer outfit set for EVE, Adam, and Lily; Half-Rim Glasses, Quadruple Rectangle Earring, Planet Diving Suit (Captain), for EVE; Stargazer & Fluffy Bear Packs for the Drone; 2,000 SP EXP; 5,000 Gold). The game will be available physically and digitally at $59.99 / £54.99 / €59.99 / ¥7,980 / ₩69,800 MSRP. The physical version of Stellar Blade Complete Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 ships with the entire game data on the cartridge: no game-key card, no additional download required to play.

articles.headline: Lufia is finally coming to PC for the first time ever
articles.summary: Taito is bringing the two original Lufia games to PC for the first time in the series’ history, as part of a four-platform collection announced overnight. The publisher confirmed Lufia I & II The...
articles.body: Taito is bringing the two original Lufia games to PC for the first time in the series’ history, as part of a four-platform collection announced overnight. The publisher confirmed Lufia I & II The Sinistrals Saga for PC, PS5, Switch 2 and Switch during the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, with a planned launch in 2027. The official Steam page lists Taito as both developer and publisher and confirms the 2027 window. The collection packages 1993’s Lufia & the Fortress of Doom and its 1995 prequel Lufia II: Rise of the Sinistrals as a single purchase. A first for a series stuck on old hardware The collection is the first official PC release for a series that previously lived only on SNES and DS hardware. The original Lufia & the Fortress of Doom released in Japan and North America in 1993 and skipped Europe entirely, and secondhand SNES cartridges of the game reportedly run into the hundreds of pounds. For players who never wanted to pay that, the Steam release is the first legitimate way to play it in decades. Taito producer Yuichi Toyama says the project began four or five years ago, after the team started looking into the rights following years of fan demand for a revival. Clear River Games will publish the collection in the west, and its producer James Wragg described the goal as “emulation as close to the original game as possible”. What’s in the package Both games are being sold together, so the whole Sinistrals story is playable without hunting a physical copy. Lufia II is the prequel in story terms despite the numbering, and follows Maxim, a young man who would later be hailed as a hero of legend, and his companions’ battle against destiny. Its 99-floor, procedurally generated Ancient Cave, which resets players to level one, is cited by Taito as pioneering roguelike design decades before the genre went mainstream. A physical release has been confirmed, though the detail so far applies to the Switch versions. No Australian price has been announced, and no specific release date beyond the 2027 window. One oddity: the Steam wishlist page at one stage showed a date of 16 November 2026, which conflicts with every stated 2027 figure; the store page itself says 2027. Wishlist it and wait, or keep an eye out closer to the date.

articles.headline: Petrobras Backs New Diesel Subsidy as Fuel Payments Reach $1.9 Billion
articles.summary: Home Energy Company News By Charles Kennedy - Sep 20, 2026, 8:56 PM CDT Brazilian state-controlled oil giant Petrobras said it received R$448...
articles.body: Home Energy Company News By Charles Kennedy - Sep 20, 2026, 8:56 PM CDT Brazilian state-controlled oil giant Petrobras said it received R$448 million ($85 million) under a federal gasoline subsidy program, pushing the company's cumulative receipts from government fuel-support measures to R$9.9 billion, or roughly $1.9 billion. The latest payment covers gasoline sold between July 16 and July 31 under Provisional Measure 1,358, Petrobras said. The legislation created temporary subsidies for petroleum-derived fuels in response to the impact of international energy-market disruptions. The R$9.9 billion total includes subsidies paid to Petrobras for diesel, gasoline and liquefied petroleum gas. The gasoline program itself has since expired. Provisional Measure 1,358 ceased to be effective on September 9, according to Brazil's Congress, prompting Petrobras to discontinue a R$0.44-per-liter gasoline discount from September 10. At the same time, Brazil is expanding support for diesel. Petrobras said its board approved participation in a new subsidy established under Provisional Measure 1,391, which covers producers and importers of road diesel. The program provides R$1.00 per liter of diesel A for 30 days, with the possibility of extending the measure for another 30 days. The new subsidy is designed to support diesel supply during instability linked to geopolitical disruptions, according to the legislation. Crucially for Petrobras, the new program can operate alongside an earlier diesel subsidy under Provisional Measure 1,363, which provides R$1.12 per liter. Petrobras said benefits under the two programs are cumulative, potentially giving eligible volumes support from both mechanisms. Petrobras has already adjusted its diesel pricing mechanism following the introduction of the new R$1.00 subsidy. From September 17, the company raised its diesel A sales price to distributors by R$1.00 per liter while simultaneously applying an equivalent subsidy-backed discount, leaving the effective price impact offset by the government support. Formal participation in the latest program remains subject to the applicable regulatory process, Petrobras said. The subsidies give Petrobras another buffer against sharp international fuel-price movements while allowing Brazil to limit their immediate transmission into domestic prices. The company said its commercial strategy continues to focus on market share, refinery optimization and profitability rather than automatically passing short-term changes in international prices and exchange rates through to Brazilian consumers. For investors, the rising subsidy payments are significant because they allow government fuel-price support to be financed through the federal budget rather than requiring Petrobras itself to absorb the full cost of below-market discounts. articles.headline: Discarded pool chemicals in garbage truck load cause vapor cloud, hours-long hazmat response in Gurnee
articles.summary: A garbage truck dumped its load into a parking lot on the northwest corner of Washington Street and Ambrogio Drive in Gurnee after the driver thought a fire had started, which turned out to be a hazardous...
articles.body: A garbage truck dumped its load into a parking lot on the northwest corner of Washington Street and Ambrogio Drive in Gurnee after the driver thought a fire had started, which turned out to be a hazardous materials incident involving chemicals that mixed together. | Photo Submitted to Lake and McHenry County Scanner Discarded pool chemicals that got wet in a garbage truck load caused a vapor cloud, prompting an hours-long hazardous materials response and a shelter-in-place notice in Gurnee. The Gurnee Fire Department and Gurnee Police Department responded around 10:53 a.m. Thursday to the area of Washington Street and Ambrogio Drive in Gurnee for a report of a vehicle fire. Gurnee Fire Department Battalion Chief Tim Steffens said crews arrived to find a Waste Management garbage truck that had dumped its load, which is common practice when there is a potential fire. Fire crews found light smoke coming from the garbage debris in the dentist office parking lot on the northwest corner of the intersection. Firefighters began extinguishing the pile with water but they heard crackling and popping sounds and smelled a strange odor, Steffens said. Additional fire department resources were requested to the scene and the area was secured. Steffens said firefighters found five crushed buckets, covered in debris, containing substances believed to be pool chemicals. The products consisted of calcium hypochlorite, chlorine granules and chlorine tablets. The chemicals were combined when they got wet and started emitting a vapor cloud, which affected an isolated area, Steffens said. Steffens said it was also ultimately determined that there was no fire as initially thought and that it was off-gassing related to the chemicals. Ambrogio Drive was shut down at Washington Street, which affected access to the businesses in the area. Steffens said first responders notified buildings in the area to shelter in place and turn off their HVAC systems. No injuries were reported and the incident did not pose an immediate danger to anyone. Waste Management called their own cleanup company, SET Environmental, which arrived in the afternoon and remained on the scene for hours, Steffens said. The Gurnee Police Department issued an alert to people in the area, saying the incident required “extended cleanup, and the roadway is expected to remain closed for several hours.” “There is no hazardous materials threat to the public. The closure is limited to this area and is not affecting traffic on surrounding major roadways,” the department said. “Please avoid the immediate area and allow emergency and cleanup crews room to work,” they added. articles.headline: The iron-air storage solution for solar
articles.summary: Priyansh Mohan, co-founder and CEO of Meine Electric, with the firm’s fast-charging iron-air battery system India’s accelerated efforts to raise renewable energy capacity in the...
articles.body: Priyansh Mohan, co-founder and CEO of Meine Electric, with the firm’s fast-charging iron-air battery system India’s accelerated efforts to raise renewable energy capacity in the coming years face at least one significant challenge — lack of mature storage technologies. Renewable power generation firms are often forced to stop production at midday, which is peak hour for solar power production, as there isn’t enough demand for such energy. Theoretically, power can be stored in largescale batteries and used when demand rises in the evenings. But the country does not have such storage capacity due to the high cost of imports and lack of indigenous technology. Producers have seen 15–20 per cent average curtailment — namely having to stop production due to lack of demand — with at least one instance of curtailment spiking to 65 per cent last year due to lack of grid-scale storage. According to Prof Aravind Kumar Chandiran, Faculty, Department of Chemical Engineering, IIT-Madras, “We see from our studies that electricity consumption is projected to triple in India from about 2,000 terawatt hour (TWh) today to about 6,000 TWh by 2047.” Iron-air battery workflow He reasons this would mean about 4 TWh of daily energy storage capacity would be needed, assuming only 50 per cent of power would come from renewables and only half of this would need storage for future use. As India cannot afford to rely only on imported lithium to meet storage demand of such magnitude, it is important to bring in alternatives, such as domestic mineral solutions. Lithium-ion batteries offer high power delivery and are quickly responsive. They are ideal for electric mobility and transient, high-power grid spikes. Metal-air technologies (such as iron-air or zinc-air) offer low power delivery but for a longer duration. These are best suited for steady-state grid storage. Unlike lithium-ion battery manufacturing, which requires expensive, highly controlled clean-room and ultra-dry environments to prevent chemical instability, iron-air systems can be fabricated in ambient atmospheric conditions, drastically reducing production and capital expenses. Metal-air systems suffer from what is called ‘high electrochemical overpotential’ — they need more voltage during a reaction, such as the charging or discharging of a battery. This results in significantly lower efficiency compared to lithium-ion technology. For example, iron-air yields an efficiency of 23–50 per cent, while for zinc-air it is 40–80 per cent, according to Prof Chandiran. Notably, he mentors this field directly, with three of his former PhD students having founded a start-up focused on commercialising indigenous zinc-air battery technology for stationary grid storage. Further, lithium-ion battery is a mature technology, whereas metal-air batteries still face chemistry hurdles, engineering scaling challenges and a lack of long-term real-world testing. Long-duration storage Startup Meine Electric disclosed in July that it had developed the world’s first fast-charging iron-air battery system. This could likely offer a breakthrough in long-duration energy storage. Iron-air batteries generally operate on a basic reduction-oxidation mechanism — iron reacts with oxygen and water during discharge to form iron oxide, releasing electrical energy. Reversing this reaction forces the iron oxide back into metallic iron. “Traditional iron-air systems are restricted to multi-day cycles, making them largely incompatible with the intermittent nature of renewable energy generation,” says Priyansh Mohan, Co-founder and CEO of Meine Electric. “Solar-heavy grids don’t need a 100-hour battery. Unlike regions that require seasonal storage, the renewable challenge across Asia is fundamentally a daily balancing problem.” He says Meine has engineered its system to capture a full charge within a six- to eight-hour window. This has helped compress the multi-day charging window to six hours, paired with 18 hours of discharging. The company says its technology has been tested and validated by the Customized Energy Solutions (CES) Battery Laboratory. The lab confirmed the “operational stability, capacity retention and electrochemical performance under this 6/18-hour cycle”, Meine stated. According to Mohan, using Meine’s proprietary technology, the storage cost over the battery’s lifetime would be about ₹5 per kWh. The clincher here is as much the low cost of operation as the raw material iron, as India has an abundance of iron ore and is the fourth-largest producer globally. However, there is still a long way to go before indigenous and inexpensive technologies see widespread use. According to a report on the iron-air market released by datamintelligence in August, “The market continues in validation stage. Lack of commercial operational experience, bankability issues, lack of warranty confidence and performance assurance could hinder adoption in the near term.” Prof Chandiran concurs. “Metal-air technologies will require about five years to prove themselves fit for largescale use. They need to be tested in the real world over thousands of charge-discharge cycles. There are engineering hurdles, scale hurdles, issues with lack of operational experience at scale, all of which we have to surmount.” Published on September 21, 2026

articles.headline: COMMENT | Govt must reveal reasons for Najib's pardon
articles.summary: COMMENT | We, the members of G25, are once again deeply shocked and dismayed by the decision of the Pardons Board to grant a further conditional pardon to former prime minister Najib Abdul Razak.The latest...
articles.body: COMMENT | We, the members of G25, are once again deeply shocked and dismayed by the decision of the Pardons Board to grant a further conditional pardon to former prime minister Najib Abdul Razak. The latest conditional pardon allows him to serve the remainder of his custodial sentence under house arrest if he pays his RM50 million fine. This follows the Pardons Board’s decision in 2024 to halve his 12-year prison sentence to six years and reduce his RM210 million fine to RM50 million, an astounding 76 percent reduction. In 2024, we called for the Pardons Board to provide the public with written reasons for its decision to reduce Najib’s sentence, or at the very least the written opinion of the attorney-general under Article 42(9) of the Federal Constitution. Given the serious and egregious nature of the offences involving RM42 million in SRC International funds, the substantial reduction of Najib’s sentence and fine, despite his several other criminal cases pending at the time, amounted to a travesty of the justice system. READ MORE: Najib's conditional pardon only applies to SRC International case - AG No small potato Even without his subsequent 1MDB conviction involving RM2.3 billion in December 2025, involving 21 counts of money laundering and four counts of abuse of power, the gravity of the SRC offences alone cannot be understated. Najib ( above ) was convicted on seven charges involving abuse of power, criminal breach of trust, and money laundering in relation to RM42 million in SRC International funds. This was neither a minor offence nor were the facts of the case uncertain after the trial. The SRC case took more than four years to conclude. It was not a decision made in haste. From the first charges in July 2018, through the High Court trial and judgment in July 2020, the Court of Appeal’s decision to uphold his conviction in December 2021, and finally the Federal Court’s dismissal of the appeal in August 2022, Najib was afforded the full and meticulous judicial process of our courts, and exhausted every legal avenue of appeal available to him. In upholding his conviction, the Court of Appeal also made clear the seriousness with which it viewed the SRC case. The presiding judge, Abdul Karim Abdul Jalil, said that the flow of the RM42 million into the former prime minister’s personal accounts could not be regarded as being in the national interest. “There is no national interest here, just a national embarrassment,” Karim said. Those were not the words of political opponents or commentators. They were the words from our Court of Appeal in a unanimous decision upholding his conviction. They should not have been forgotten when considering the extraordinary leniency that has since been extended to Najib. The public deserves an answer Two years after his imprisonment, he received his first partial pardon with a reduced jail term and fine. Yet, another two years later, it appears that the concerns raised over his initial partial pardon have fallen on deaf ears, with clemency now extended in the form of a house arrest order to a former prime minister whose guilt was unequivocally established by the highest court in the land. For us in G25, this house arrest order is the unkindest cut of all, and we believe the vast majority of the rakyat feel the same. This does nothing to strengthen public confidence in our criminal justice system. It is a travesty of justice. It is difficult for the public to reconcile this repeated reduction in punishment with the government’s stated commitment to strengthening the rule of law and combating corruption. The government must take this loss of public trust seriously. A conviction reached after the judicial process has been exhausted must carry meaning. While the constitutional power of clemency provides an important safeguard, its exercise should not leave the public with the impression that the consequences of a final conviction can be repeatedly and substantially reduced without transparent reasons being given. With regard to the law, Article 42(9) of the Federal Constitution provides that the Pardons Board shall consider the written opinion of the attorney-general. In addition, Article 40(1A) states that the Yang di-Pertuan Agong must act on the advice of the Pardons Board. In Najib’s case, the public should be provided with the written opinion of the AG and the representation of the federal territories minister, Hannah Yeoh. It should be made clear whether the decision to grant house arrest was consistent with the written advice of the AG and the representation made by the minister. If so, the public should be told. If not, the public is equally entitled to know. No such thing as house arrest, legally In addition, the recent case of Dato’ Sri Mohd Najib Tun Hj Abd Razak v Menteri Dalam Negeri [2026] 2 MLRH 387, where judge Alice Loke held that a house arrest order is not capable of execution , there being no legal provision for such a mechanism, is highly relevant. In her judgment, Loke said (p.408): “[68] In any event, I am of the view that a house arrest order is not capable of execution, there being no legal provision for such mechanism in Malaysia.” This is not a matter of legal theory. It is a direct judicial finding that, at the time of judgment, Malaysian law did not (and still does not) provide a mechanism for house arrest. In light of this, we are concerned about what legal advice was given to the Pardons Board. An explanation is needed to clearly explain what has changed in the law, or what legal authority now exists, to form the basis of its decision to order the house arrest. The decision also raises the question of equal treatment under the law. The law is no respecter of persons, and Article 8 of the Federal Constitution guarantees equality before the law. The rule of law requires that justice be administered fairly and consistently, regardless of a person’s position, wealth or former office. If house arrest is to become part of Malaysia’s criminal justice system, it should be governed by clear and generally applicable laws and criteria, rather than appearing to have been created, in effect, for the benefit of one particular individual. Legal experts have also noted that this appears to be an unprecedented use of house arrest as a form of royal clemency in Malaysia. Higher office, worse punishment The public is entitled to ask a simple question: would the same treatment be available to an ordinary prisoner convicted of comparable offences? If the answer is no, the government must explain what principle of equal justice justifies the distinction. If the argument for additional clemency through house arrest is based on the high public office a person once held, as public perception may assume in this case, logic would suggest that the opposite is more justified. There is a strong basis for the view that a person who abuses the powers and responsibilities entrusted to him by virtue of a high public office should, rather than receive more lenient treatment, be held to an even higher standard of accountability and, where appropriate, face a more severe punishment. The precedent of greater leniency for offences committed by those holding higher offices is deeply troubling. This is because the consequences of abuse in those positions are not limited to the individual and those affected alone, but extend to the integrity of public institutions, the stability of the nation and the peace of its people. For this reason, public office should never become a shield against the full consequences of wrongdoing. If anything, the greater the power entrusted to a person, the greater the obligation to account for its abuse. We, the members of G25, reiterate our call for full transparency regarding the reasons and constitutional basis for this latest decision by the Pardons Board, to avoid public speculation and to ensure clarity in our laws and confidence in the justice system. The public should not be left to piece together the constitutional and legal basis of an extraordinary decision from media reports, statements, and speculation. Given the seriousness of this matter and the damage it has done to Malaysia’s domestic and international standing, G25 also calls upon the Pardons Board to urgently revisit this decision at its earliest possible meeting, with a view to rescinding the further clemency granted to Najib. ‘Just accept’ adds insult to injury Our current government has repeatedly pledged to strengthen the rule of law, combat corruption, and restore confidence in our public institutions. However, the strength of the government’s commitment to reform is ultimately measured not only by its words and policies, but by what it does when those principles are tested. Recent comments from Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on the house arrest order, as reported in Malay Mail Online on Sept 18, quoted him saying, “... ultimately, the Constitution provides for the powers of His Majesty the King, and I hope we can accept the decision...” With respect, is this all our prime minister has to say? Is Anwar so removed from the rakyat that he could not fathom the deep feeling of hurt, humiliation, and cruel injustice felt by the vast majority of the citizens? Respect for the constitutional role of the king does not mean that the government, or the public, should be expected to remain silent on questions of legality, transparency, and justice to the citizens. Telling the public to simply “accept the decision” is not an adequate answer to legitimate questions about a decision of such profound importance to the rule of law. It is akin to adding insult to injury. It risks conveying the very message the government should be working to dispel - that accountability applies differently depending on who is involved. The government cannot, on the one hand, tell Malaysians that corruption and abuse of power must never be taken lightly, while on the other hand asking them to simply accept an extraordinary reduction in the consequences faced by a former prime minister convicted of serious corruption-related offences that robbed our country and its rakyat of public funds meant for their benefit. Do not insult the people’s intelligence These are not merely matters of political rhetoric. They concern the credibility of our institutions and whether Malaysians can have confidence that the law applies without fear or favour. If the Madani government is serious about restoring confidence in our public institutions, then the solution towards that goal in this instance is extremely simple. raw_detail.incipit: COMMENT | We, the members of G25, are once again deeply shocked and dismayed by the decision of the Pardons Board to grant a further conditional pardon to former prime minister Najib Abdul Razak.The latest...
raw_detail.body: COMMENT | We, the members of G25, are once again deeply shocked and dismayed by the decision of the Pardons Board to grant a further conditional pardon to former prime minister Najib Abdul Razak. The latest conditional pardon allows him to serve the remainder of his custodial sentence under house arrest if he pays his RM50 million fine. This follows the Pardons Board’s decision in 2024 to halve his 12-year prison sentence to six years and reduce his RM210 million fine to RM50 million, an astounding 76 percent reduction. In 2024, we called for the Pardons Board to provide the public with written reasons for its decision to reduce Najib’s sentence, or at the very least the written opinion of the attorney-general under Article 42(9) of the Federal Constitution. Given the serious and egregious nature of the offences involving RM42 million in SRC International funds, the substantial reduction of Najib’s sentence and fine, despite his several other criminal cases pending at the time, amounted to a travesty of the justice system. READ MORE: Najib's conditional pardon only applies to SRC International case - AG No small potato Even without his subsequent 1MDB conviction involving RM2.3 billion in December 2025, involving 21 counts of money laundering and four counts of abuse of power, the gravity of the SRC offences alone cannot be understated. Najib ( above ) was convicted on seven charges involving abuse of power, criminal breach of trust, and money laundering in relation to RM42 million in SRC International funds. This was neither a minor offence nor were the facts of the case uncertain after the trial. The SRC case took more than four years to conclude. It was not a decision made in haste. From the first charges in July 2018, through the High Court trial and judgment in July 2020, the Court of Appeal’s decision to uphold his conviction in December 2021, and finally the Federal Court’s dismissal of the appeal in August 2022, Najib was afforded the full and meticulous judicial process of our courts, and exhausted every legal avenue of appeal available to him. In upholding his conviction, the Court of Appeal also made clear the seriousness with which it viewed the SRC case. The presiding judge, Abdul Karim Abdul Jalil, said that the flow of the RM42 million into the former prime minister’s personal accounts could not be regarded as being in the national interest. “There is no national interest here, just a national embarrassment,” Karim said. Those were not the words of political opponents or commentators. They were the words from our Court of Appeal in a unanimous decision upholding his conviction. They should not have been forgotten when considering the extraordinary leniency that has since been extended to Najib. The public deserves an answer Two years after his imprisonment, he received his first partial pardon with a reduced jail term and fine. Yet, another two years later, it appears that the concerns raised over his initial partial pardon have fallen on deaf ears, with clemency now extended in the form of a house arrest order to a former prime minister whose guilt was unequivocally established by the highest court in the land. For us in G25, this house arrest order is the unkindest cut of all, and we believe the vast majority of the rakyat feel the same. This does nothing to strengthen public confidence in our criminal justice system. It is a travesty of justice. It is difficult for the public to reconcile this repeated reduction in punishment with the government’s stated commitment to strengthening the rule of law and combating corruption. The government must take this loss of public trust seriously. A conviction reached after the judicial process has been exhausted must carry meaning. While the constitutional power of clemency provides an important safeguard, its exercise should not leave the public with the impression that the consequences of a final conviction can be repeatedly and substantially reduced without transparent reasons being given. With regard to the law, Article 42(9) of the Federal Constitution provides that the Pardons Board shall consider the written opinion of the attorney-general. In addition, Article 40(1A) states that the Yang di-Pertuan Agong must act on the advice of the Pardons Board. In Najib’s case, the public should be provided with the written opinion of the AG and the representation of the federal territories minister, Hannah Yeoh. It should be made clear whether the decision to grant house arrest was consistent with the written advice of the AG and the representation made by the minister. If so, the public should be told. If not, the public is equally entitled to know. No such thing as house arrest, legally In addition, the recent case of Dato’ Sri Mohd Najib Tun Hj Abd Razak v Menteri Dalam Negeri [2026] 2 MLRH 387, where judge Alice Loke held that a house arrest order is not capable of execution , there being no legal provision for such a mechanism, is highly relevant. In her judgment, Loke said (p.408): “[68] In any event, I am of the view that a house arrest order is not capable of execution, there being no legal provision for such mechanism in Malaysia.” This is not a matter of legal theory. It is a direct judicial finding that, at the time of judgment, Malaysian law did not (and still does not) provide a mechanism for house arrest. In light of this, we are concerned about what legal advice was given to the Pardons Board. An explanation is needed to clearly explain what has changed in the law, or what legal authority now exists, to form the basis of its decision to order the house arrest. The decision also raises the question of equal treatment under the law. The law is no respecter of persons, and Article 8 of the Federal Constitution guarantees equality before the law. The rule of law requires that justice be administered fairly and consistently, regardless of a person’s position, wealth or former office. If house arrest is to become part of Malaysia’s criminal justice system, it should be governed by clear and generally applicable laws and criteria, rather than appearing to have been created, in effect, for the benefit of one particular individual. Legal experts have also noted that this appears to be an unprecedented use of house arrest as a form of royal clemency in Malaysia. Higher office, worse punishment The public is entitled to ask a simple question: would the same treatment be available to an ordinary prisoner convicted of comparable offences? If the answer is no, the government must explain what principle of equal justice justifies the distinction. If the argument for additional clemency through house arrest is based on the high public office a person once held, as public perception may assume in this case, logic would suggest that the opposite is more justified. There is a strong basis for the view that a person who abuses the powers and responsibilities entrusted to him by virtue of a high public office should, rather than receive more lenient treatment, be held to an even higher standard of accountability and, where appropriate, face a more severe punishment. The precedent of greater leniency for offences committed by those holding higher offices is deeply troubling. This is because the consequences of abuse in those positions are not limited to the individual and those affected alone, but extend to the integrity of public institutions, the stability of the nation and the peace of its people. For this reason, public office should never become a shield against the full consequences of wrongdoing. If anything, the greater the power entrusted to a person, the greater the obligation to account for its abuse. We, the members of G25, reiterate our call for full transparency regarding the reasons and constitutional basis for this latest decision by the Pardons Board, to avoid public speculation and to ensure clarity in our laws and confidence in the justice system. articles.headline: In Washington, temples to Trump’s ego lie ruined. And another is on the way
articles.summary: September 21, 2026 — 11:49amIt was deathly quiet outside the John F. Kennedy Memorial Centre for the Performing Arts on Friday afternoon. Ordinarily, the storied cultural institution would have been preparing...
articles.body: September 21, 2026 — 11:49am It was deathly quiet outside the John F. Kennedy Memorial Centre for the Performing Arts on Friday afternoon. Ordinarily, the storied cultural institution would have been preparing for an evening of performances: an opera, perhaps, or musical theatre. Instead, the building was closed, its white Italian marble exterior surrounded by scaffolding, temporary chain-link fences and security guards patrolling the perimeter. Scaffolding covers the signage where a court ordered the Trump administration to remove Donald Trump’s name. AP The Kennedy Centre – so named for the assassinated Democratic president – was abruptly shuttered last week following a vote by its board. The board is chaired by President Donald Trump, who gutted the previous board and installed loyalists with the explicit intent of making him chair. The centre’s closure did not change much, in practical terms. The only programming on Friday night was a free, unticketed show by “master illusionist” Michael Grandinetti, which proceeded at an expansion site outside the main Kennedy Centre building. That is because artists and arts lovers have largely given the Kennedy Centre a wide berth since Trump began taking over the venue last year and had his name inscribed on the side of the building. Performers cancelled shows, donors withdrew and ticket sales nosedived. Last October, The Washington Post calculated 43 per cent of tickets remained unsold for the typical autumn production. Things have only worsened since. Staff and programs have been slashed, and the budget is in disarray. Protesters on Friday night linked hands to form a human chain around the Kennedy Centre. AP This giant of American cultural life – and a living memorial to one of the country’s slain presidents – now lies empty and sad. It is a cautionary tale; a temple to the tragedy of ego. The stalemate may continue. Trump secured the money, $US257 million, from Congress for a major two-year renovation, which he and his board argue is sorely needed. But he is refusing to begin the work unless he can put his name back on the building. It’s not just his name; court documents show Trump is insisting on three things. One is changing the plaque on the front of the building to read: “The John F. Kennedy Memorial Centre for the Performing Arts, renovated and restored by President Donald J. Trump.” Second, when his Trump Kennedy Centre Fund reaches an endowment of $US100 million, he proposes to add: “Endowed by the Trump Kennedy Centre Fund” to the plaque. Finally, he wants to name the surrounding area “President Donald J. Trump Plaza”. The board approved these proposals last month. The Reflecting Pool outside the Lincoln Memorial remains drained and fenced off to visitors. AP Last week, a federal judge appointed by Barack Obama, Christopher Cooper, put a stop to this. He is the same judge who last year ordered Trump’s name be taken off the building, as Congress had named it in honour of President Kennedy alone. Now, Cooper said, the administration “plays word games” to try to skirt the ruling. “Alone means alone,” Cooper ruled. “The board cannot honour both President Kennedy and President Trump without running afoul of the terms of the injunction and the board’s own governing statute.” Trump has defended this narcissism by arguing he is saving the Kennedy Centre from certain ruin. He says he raised the $US257 million from Congress himself (“they gave it to me because it’s me”) and would have to keep raising funds after he leaves office because the centre has always lost money. “That place is a dump. It’s been a dump for years. I’m ready to fix it,” he said. “I think the Trump administration should be recognised as having saved the Kennedy Centre because nobody else can do it.” US President Donald Trump spoke about the Kennedy Centre last week, with John F. Kennedy’s nephew, Robert F. Kennedy Jr, behind him. AP One may well scoff at the idea of Trump, who somehow paid no income tax for many years, fundraising for the arts after he departs the White House. And if the centre was such a dangerous “dump”, why was it chosen to host the FIFA World Cup draw late last year, a major event attended by Trump, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and FIFA president Gianni Infantino? The building may be deserving of a renovation – and nobody is opposing that – but there’s no doubt Trump and his acolytes have milked that for all it’s worth. When a five-foot piece of ceiling plaster collapsed during a storm this month, the debris wasn’t cleaned up: as The New York Times reported on Sunday , staff “left the mess on the carpet for nearly two weeks”, documenting it as part of a brief on the building’s decay. One need not venture far to see another victim of Trump’s egomania. Down at the National Mall, the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is still blocked off by fencing – more than two months after it was drained again to repair a botched job by the contractor. Trump says the “Triumphal Arch” he intends to build across the river near Arlington Cemetery will have snipers and be stocked with ammunition. Bloomberg No work was being done on Saturday morning when this masthead visited, although bobcats and trailers sat strewn around the pool’s barren surface and on the nearby grass. What was once a rush job to be finished for Independence Day is now languishing in the incomplete basket. And across the river, Trump has just announced that his planned Triumphal Arch will be stuffed with drones, snipers and ammunition, turning it into a “military complex”. This was apparently at the military’s request, despite the Pentagon being a stone’s throw away. There is an obvious reason for this change – Trump has learnt from the White House ballroom that declaring something a security necessity can generate a lot of leverage. The courts allowed him to continue work on the underground military parts of the ballroom while pausing work on the above-ground sections. Washington is a grand city of monuments to American endeavour and excellence. This president wishes to turn them into monuments to his own ego, or, as things stand, leave them to rot when he cannot get his way. articles.summary: KINI SNAPSHOT | What’s going on in the news today, with updates at 9am, 2pm, 6pm, and 9pm.9amPolitics- Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim denied paving the way for a conditional pardon for former premier Najib...
articles.body: KINI SNAPSHOT | What’s going on in the news today, with updates at 9am, 2pm, 6pm, and 9pm. 9am Politics - Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim denied paving the way for a conditional pardon for former premier Najib Abdul Razak. Affirming that the pardon does not affect legal proceedings involving other cases, Anwar stressed that every prisoner, including Najib, has a right to submit an appeal to the Pardons Board. Bernama quoted him as detailing the matter when speaking to reporters on the sidelines of a Perintis Reformis reunion in Shah Alam yesterday. Previously, Anwar helped fast-track Najib’s first pardon hearing under the previous Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s reign, which led to the former premier’s SRC International sentence being significantly reduced. - Anwar took the time to celebrate Malacca Chief Minister Ab Rauf Yusoh’s birthday with him in the state yesterday. The prime minister also shared videos of the event on his social media pages, with clips showing Anwar singing "happy birthday" to Rauf in front of a cake. In a separate post, Rauf thanked Anwar for the gesture, noting that while their political thoughts might differ, mutual respect and efforts to prioritise the rakyat remain present. Anwar’s Pakatan Harapan has been trying to work out a deal for electoral cooperation with Malacca BN for the upcoming state polls.

articles.headline: Putin's United Russia wins tightly controlled wartime election
articles.summary: The Kremlin-backed United Russia party has secured victory in Russia's parliamentary election, taking more than half of the vote, according to preliminary results reported by Russian news agencies.United...
articles.body: The Kremlin-backed United Russia party has secured victory in Russia's parliamentary election, taking more than half of the vote, according to preliminary results reported by Russian news agencies. United Russia secured 57.9% of the vote after more than 50% of ballots have been counted, Interfax reported, citing the election commission. Predictions had placed the party, which has ruled for more than 20 years, below 50%. According to preliminary estimates, the party was set to win 309 of the 450 seats in the State Duma, including direct mandates, nine more seats than are needed to amend the constitution, Novaya Gazeta reported. The election was Russia's first parliamentary vote since President Vladimir Putin launched the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and was widely seen as a test of public backing for the war. The vote has been dismissed by democracy watchdogs, Western governments and Kremlin opponents as neither free nor fair, with critics accusing the authorities of excluding genuine opposition and tightly controlling the political landscape. The anti-war Yabloko party was barred from the election, while all parties represented in the outgoing parliament are considered loyal to the Kremlin and support Russia's war against Ukraine. The Communist Party won 13.8% of the vote, followed by the ultranationalist LDPR on 8.8% and New People on 7.9%, according to the initial results. A Just Russia was on 5.1%, putting all four parties on course to return to the State Duma. Official figures put turnout at more than 56%, higher than in the 2021 parliamentary election. Figures provided by Russia's electoral authorities cannot be independently verified. Despite Ukraine's protests, the election was held for the first time in the Russian-controlled parts of the annexed Ukrainian regions of Luhansk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhya and Kherson. The Black Sea peninsula of Crimea, which was annexed back in 2014, was once again included. Allegations of electoral violations Yabloko, which was initially approved to stand before being removed from the ballot, and the traditionally strong Communist Party both complained that hundreds of their observers had been prevented from monitoring polling stations. Civil servants also reported being pressured to vote, while there were allegations of ballot stuffing, as in previous Russian elections. Some voters complained that they had not received polling cards and had been registered for online voting without their knowledge. Electronic voting in Russia has faced criticism over a lack of transparency and concerns about possible manipulation. More than 110 million Russians were eligible to elect the 450 members of the new State Duma in the three-day vote. In addition to the Duma election, deputies were also elected to regional parliaments in eight regions. According to the election commission, a total of around 2,200 elections took place at various levels of government.
