articles.headline: Princess Diana's brother says his bombshell claims against King Charles following her death will 'not be a surprise' to nephews William and Harry
articles.summary: Princess Diana’s brother Earl Spencer insinuated that he’d already spoken to his nephews, Prince William and Prince Harry, about the bombshell claims he makes about her death in his upcoming book. Spencer...
articles.body: Princess Diana’s brother Earl Spencer insinuated that he’d already spoken to his nephews, Prince William and Prince Harry, about the bombshell claims he makes about her death in his upcoming book. Spencer told the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg in his interview Friday , “I don’t like to talk about what I’ve been speaking about to William and Harry, but this will not be a surprise to them.” “I will tell you that these words will not be a surprise to them,” he insisted. Spencer’s comments echo what an insider told Page Six last week about Harry’s reaction to his uncle’s claims about his mom’s death in his upcoming book, “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister.” Princess Diana’s brother Earl Spencer said in an interview with the BBC that his nephews, Prince William and Prince Harry, won’t be surprised by his bombshell claims about her death in his upcoming book. BBC Spencer told the BBC’s Lauren Kuennsberg, “I will tell you that these words will not be a surprise to them.” via REUTERS “It didn’t come as a shock,” a source in the know told us. We’re told the two actually discussed the book during Harry’s visit to the Spencer ancestral estate, Althorp, back in July when he brought his wife, Meghan Markle, and their kids — Princess Lilibet, 5, and Prince Archie, 7 — to see his mother’s burial site. In Spencer’s highly anticipated new book, he alleges King Charles III told him that Diana would be forgotten “soon enough” in a horrific phone call following her death in 1997. “He unleashed down the phone what I have always taken to be his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death,” Spencer claimed, per an excerpt obtained by the Daily Mail. “’Rest assured,’” he hissed, ‘we’ll forget her soon enough!’” In his book, “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister,” Spencer claims King Charles III told him that Diana would be forgotten “soon enough” after her tragic death. Diana and Charles are seen here in February 1981. Getty Images Diana tragically died after a horrific car crash in 1997. Spencer, William, Harry and Charles are seen here at her funeral. Getty Images Spencer said he was in disbelief at the time and hung up the phone. He also alleged that Charles “sounded giddily elated — like a lottery winner” after his ex-wife died. “Looking back now, I suspect the prince’s first reaction must have been to think more of how this event might free him to marry the woman he loved, rather than appreciating the loss of one he did not,” Spencer mused, referring to now-Queen Camilla, whom Charles wed in 2005 . But 77-year-old Charles — who had a famously tumultuous marriage to Diana from 1981 until they split in 1992, and finalized their divorce four years later — has hit back at Spencer’s claims. Spencer also claims in his book that Charles sounded “giddily elated” after Diana died. Charles and Diana are pictured here on their wedding day in July 1981. AP Charles and Diana had a rocky marriage for 11 years before they split in 1992. Tim Graham Photo Library via Getty Images A rep for Buckingham Palace told Page Six, “While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss.” Spencer, 62, doubled down on his claims in his interview with Kuenssberg, insisting he was “telling the truth.” “I can tell you here and now, those are exactly the words he said,” he stressed. “I was hyper alert to what he was saying and those are precisely the words that he said and I promise that to you now. Genuinely, that is what he said. I don’t hear him saying he didn’t say that.” Although Charles has hit back at his claims, Spencer insisted to the BBC that he’s “telling the truth.” charles.earl.spencer/instagram “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister” is out Tuesday in the UK and the US. Amer Ghazzal/Shutterstock “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister” is out Tuesday in both the UK and the US. Spencer also told the BBC that he sees parallels between how his late sister was treated and with how Harry, 42, and Markle, 45, are treated by the public. “If you look at an article in a tabloid about Diana or the couple that you’re mentioning, Harry and Meghan, they can be really, really unpleasant,” Spencer said. “I think it would be really beholden on people to learn from Diana’s example,” he continued, referencing her tragic death following a car crash in Paris at age 36. articles.headline: Ukraine war briefing: Russia to ‘intensify’ attacks on Kyiv after Moscow hit with mass drone strikes
articles.summary: Russia has vowed to “intensify” its strikes on Kyiv while accusing Ukraine of attempting to “disrupt” Russian elections after Ukraine fired waves of drones at the Moscow region on the final day of voting,...
articles.body: Russia has vowed to “intensify” its strikes on Kyiv while accusing Ukraine of attempting to “disrupt” Russian elections after Ukraine fired waves of drones at the Moscow region on the final day of voting, killing at least two people. “In response to the Kyiv regime’s attacks on civilian targets within Russia, the Russian army will continue and intensify its high-accuracy strikes against military targets in Kyiv,” the Russian defence ministry said. The attack was the largest on Moscow since the Kremlin launched its Ukraine offensive in 2022 and involved about 1,600 drones , 450 of which were aimed directly at the capital, Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin said. Images showed a gaping hole in a multi-storey apartment building on the outskirts of Moscow. Another showed black smoke pouring from what appeared to be an oil refinery. Volodymyr Zelenskyy praised Ukraine’s attacks , saying: “Our long-range responses had a very significant impact in the Moscow region last night.” The Ukrainian presidient said that among the weapons used in the attack was the Pelican , initially thought to be a short-range ballistic missile, but which sources said later was a winged drone. Zelenskyy said also Ukraine had used its domestically produced Flamingo cruise missiles to strike Moscow. The long-range weapon has previously been used against targets deep inside Russia . Preliminary results from Russia’s election, released by the country’s election commission early Monday, showed the main Kremlin party dominating the vote . The tightly controlled balloting was virtually devoid of opposition to President Vladimir Putin’s policies and all but certain to cement the Kremlin’s dominance. With about 58% of the precincts counted, United Russia had nearly 58% of the vote for the 225 deputies apportioned by party lists, according to the Central Election Commission. The balloting included residents of four Ukrainian regions that Moscow illegally annexed after the war began , but still doesn’t fully control, as well as those in Crimea, the Black Sea peninsula that was illegally annexed by Russia in 2014, in what Kyiv denounced as illegal and the European Union described as a “blatant violation of international law”. Zelenskyy ⁠said on Sunday he had spoken with US President Donald Trump and ⁠the two ⁠agreed ​to meet in New York for talks that “could change a lot” ⁠in terms of finding a resolution to the war with Russia. The two ⁠leaders will be in New York this week ‌for the UN ‌General Assembly. “There are ideas for de-escalation steps and for addressing fundamental security issues – energy security, food security, and the protection of human ⁠life,” Zelenskyy posted on X. European intelligence officials have raised the possibility of an imminent Russian test of Nato, Sean Walker writes , with one saying a potential attack could come in a matter of “months, not years” . The warnings come after Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, told parliament that intelligence assessments suggested Russia might launch an attack with drones or missiles on Nato territory in the coming months, as part of efforts to prove that “article 5 is more theoretical than practical”. Egypt, one of the world’s largest importers of wheat, is diversifying its source of wheat imports towards France ⁠and other European suppliers, moving away from Ukraine and Russia where supplies have been ⁠disrupted , supply minister ⁠Sherif ​Farouk was quoted as saying on Sunday. The minister’s remarks were quoted by television ⁠host Ahmed Moussa and later confirmed by a ministry spokesperson. An overnight Russian attack on the Kyiv region ⁠killed four people, including three children , Kyiv regional authorities said on Sunday. Drone attacks persisted in Kyiv and the surrounding ⁠region throughout the day. Drone fragments fell in various districts in the capital. Outside the capital, a mother and ⁠her two 3-year-old children were killed in Kyiv region when a Russian drone strike hit a private home, the emergency service ⁠said. Kyiv region governor Tymur Tkachenko said a girl died in hospital after a separate ​drone strike in another district. Tkachenko ‌said the region endured ‌more than a day of hostile attacks over several areas.
